title: The City That Never Sleeps
survival_class: Safe . / Unsecure . / Low Entity Count . (three bullet lines; no numeric class stated)
physical_identity: Vast empty Western-style metropolis: block roads, skyscraper to low-rise districts, parks, subways, canals; indestructible bland buildings; unofficial hub of the Backrooms.
scale_topology: Effectively unbounded outdoor city with infinite subways; skyscrapers and underground; page gives population ~129,500.
anomalies: Goods and props noclip/change only when unobserved
1/3 of buildings unenterable with mirror-like windows
Fixed, inconspicuous one-way exits to thousands of levels
lighting_sound: Not stated: no light level, time of day or ambient sound described. Buildings have working lighting inside.

signature_mechanic: A fluid, mostly-empty hub city whose unobserved props change and whose building types are one-way doors to other levels; a pacifying 'Level 11 Effect' keeps entities mild.
verticality: Skyscraper districts, subways below, canals going underground; interiors sparse.
do_not: Do not make the city a dark liminal horror; page says Low Entity Count and a pacifying effect.
Do not give cars fuel or working engines.
Do not invent day/night or weather: not stated.
Do not treat quote boxes (diary, radio, forum) as article facts; they are TESTIMONY/in-universe artifacts.
Do not make every building enterable: 1/3 are not (the Capital's remodelled territory is the exception).
Do not connect Level 790 as an exit: the page calls it a dead-end level.
content_warnings: entity killing mentioned (U.E.C. kill entities on sight, incl. a young Faceling)
one entity-caused death quoted (Hoy Léi, M.E.G. explorer)
conflicts_notes: Class given as three bullets not a numeric class. Exits list notes it is non-exhaustive. Level 213 appears both as an entrance and an exit (random restaurants). Level 55 and Level 25 appear both ways.
